transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose what brings me in is that I keep thinking my wife and the kids would just be better off if I didn't wake up. It's been on my mind a lot. And lately, I've been saying out loud that I really don't need to see another winter. So, that's why I'm here.
How long have you been feeling this way—having these thoughts and this low mood?
Well, it's been going on for a while now. I'd say... since my bowling partner died. That was about a year and a month ago.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—when you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal, even if it felt good at the time?

No... no, I can't say I have. I've never been the type to bounce off the walls or go without my rest. Even before all this started, I just had my normal routine. I've never had a time where I felt unusually elated or didn't need to sleep. It's just never happened to me.
Over the past two weeks, would you say you've felt this low mood nearly every day, for most of the day?
Yes, I would say so. Every day, pretty much from the time I wake up until I go to sleep. It doesn't really lift.

Before your bowling partner passed away about a year ago, had you ever gone through a separate period in your life—say, months or years earlier—where you felt this same kind of deep sadness or hopelessness nearly every day for two weeks or more?

No... no, I don't believe so. I mean, sure, I've had sad days in the past, just regular life things. But nothing like this. Before he passed, I was doing alright. I've never had a stretch where I felt this heavy or hopeless for weeks on end. This is really the first time it's ever been like this.
